name: Sam
role: Junior data analyst, 4 months in (first job)

experience.text: Degree in statistics. Built personal projects in Python and SQL before this job.

languages.text: Spanish (native), English (professional, prefers it in writing).

communication.text: Prefers written instructions over spoken ones; spoken requests are easy to lose.
Is direct in writing; short replies can read as cold even when they are not meant to.

teamwork.text: Works best with one clear owner per task and a known person to ask.

feedback.text: Wants feedback that is specific and written down, with an example of what good looks like.

stress.text: Vague deadlines ("when you get a chance", "soon") are the main stress trigger.
Under stress, delays replying to messages instead of asking.

relationships.text: Builds trust slowly; one-to-one works better than group chats.

sensory.text: Open-plan noise after lunch is draining; noise-cancelling headphones help.

motivations.text: Clean, correct data and knowing the work is used by someone.

strengths.text: Spots patterns and errors others miss; follows processes carefully.

learning.text: Learns best from a written example, then trying it alone.
Prefers a task broken into small, concrete steps, each one saying what done looks like, so nothing is left to guess.

changes.text: Needs the why of a change first, then who to ask and by when.
Same-day changes are hard; a few days' notice makes a big difference.

adjustments.text: Instructions in writing, with an explicit deadline.
Lunch 30 minutes before the team to avoid the busy cafeteria.

managerTips.text: Follow a spoken request with a two-line message: what, by when.
